headline: Google Introduces "Beyond Zero" to Rethink Enterprise Security for AI Agents
what_happened: Google published a new enterprise-security framework, Beyond Zero, on July 27, 2026, aimed at organizations deploying AI agents alongside human employees. It extends Google's 2014 BeyondCorp zero-trust model down from whole applications to individual actions and resources, combining fixed authorization rules with real-time, dynamic risk judgments so both human and agent requests can be approved or blocked at machine speed. Google says early prototypes improved detection of access abuse.
why_it_matters: As companies give AI agents real access to internal systems, old all-or-nothing app permissions stop being enough: a compromised agent can act as fast as an attacker. Beyond Zero is Google's attempt to police each individual action agents take, not just whether they're logged in at all.
one_liner: Google built a new security system, called Beyond Zero, designed to check every single action an AI agent takes inside a company, not just whether it's allowed in the door.

citations.quote: Every single action taken inside an enterprise is authorized.
